lastAnalysis.notes:
session 1 recap (pasted from the group chat)

Brakka: Held the bridge, troll ran off, kept the goblins in line till the watch took them. Won two in the pit, lost the third to the champ — worth it.

Wick: bro rode an ox into a troll fight, lost my dagger to the river, got told the troll works for a "Toll King" 💀 also lost the party's 40g rigging dice (in my defense i was GOOD at it), Steve the ox lost a race by sitting down, and I got banned from a pie tent. 10/10 session, no notes

Maren: maren recap: rooted 3/4 goblins in place with entangle, healed brakka back up, thorn-whipped the last goblin into the burning railing (troll noped into the river lol), then patched up the surrendered goblins anyway bc soft heart. cinderford was cozy - sold out of honey, got 2nd place in the bake-off with a lavender honey loaf, and adopted a stable cat 🐈 steve the ox is now emotionally attached to me

Tovin: Tovin's night: torched a troll, lost my pit bet, and apparently 'read very well' by a woman who wants a year of my dreams for some king's secret. Also I may have quietly tidied up a loose end on the bridge — don't ask Luz about it.

Luz: Tonight Luz heal Brakka full HP after the troll fight (Cure Wounds clutch 😅), and she catch Tovin killing a goblin that was surrender, not happy about that at all. Then Ember Festival was so pretty, Luz lead the dawn blessing at the temple and whole square kneel, I nearly cry lol ✨

GM: the troll was WAY out of their league (hill troll vs lvl 3s) and they still drove it off. next session: the Toll King. rules q for next time - can Wick ride Steve as a mount without Mounted Combatant? also someone owes me pizza money

entry.name: Grovekeeper's Pantry: Lavender Loaf

mechanics.effect: Once per long rest, you can use your action to bake a simple honey loaf using foraged ingredients. This item can be sold for 5 gp or used to make a DC 10 Persuasion check to gain favor with a commoner or merchant.

lineage.rationale: Maren demonstrated skill in producing and selling honey-based goods, culminating in a competitive bake-off entry.

entry.system_equivalent: Cook's Utensils proficiency with a custom crafting action (Dungeons & Dragons Fifth Edition (2024 rules))

entry.name: Wildheart Bond: Stable Companion

mechanics.effect: You have advantage on Animal Handling checks to calm or direct a small animal you have bonded with (such as a stable cat). This animal can carry up to 5 gp of items or serve as a distraction.

lineage.rationale: Maren actively adopted a stable cat, indicating a deliberate bond with a non-combat animal companion.

entry.system_equivalent: Animal Handling proficiency with a bonded companion benefit (Dungeons & Dragons Fifth Edition (2024 rules))

entry.name: Verdant Mercy: Field Triage

mechanics.effect: Use your action to treat wounds on one creature within 5 feet. On a successful DC 10 Medicine check, the target regains 1d4 + your proficiency bonus Hit Points. If the target is a humanoid enemy who has surrendered, they also gain advantage on their next saving throw against a fear effect.

lineage.rationale: Maren consistently provided medical aid to both allies and surrendered enemies, showing a dedicated focus on field triage.

entry.system_equivalent: Medicine proficiency with a healing action (Dungeons & Dragons Fifth Edition (2024 rules))

evidence: rooted 3/4 goblins in place with entangle
thorn-whipped the last goblin into the burning railing

entry.name: Thornweave: Gnarled Snare

mechanics.effect: When a creature within 15 feet of you moves, you can use your reaction to cause thorny vines to erupt from the ground, forcing the creature to make a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, the creature is Restrained until the end of its next turn. On a success, the creature is not Restrained but has its speed reduced to 0 feet until the end of its next turn.
mechanics.trigger: A creature within 15 feet of you moves.

lineage.rationale: Maren demonstrated a distinct combat application of plant control beyond standard Entangle, using thorn-whips to physically redirect enemies into hazards. This suggests a reactive, defensive use of wild growth to control battlefield positioning.

entry.system_equivalent: Druidic reaction feat (Dungeons & Dragons Fifth Edition (2024 rules))
